iPhone 18 Pro is about to be released, and rumours suggest the Pro Max model may have unique advantages in several key areas this year. Here's a preview.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will see a more significant battery life improvement this year, and may also have an edge in the camera department

Historically, Apple has maintained a similar level of annual feature differentiation across the Pro lineup.

Beyond the Pro Max's more obvious advantages — a larger display and longer battery life — it sometimes also gets a camera feature exclusively.

For the iPhone 18 Pro this year, rumours indicate Apple will continue the same strategy.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery life was always going to outlast the iPhone 18 Pro. But according to a recent regulatory filing leak, the gap will be more pronounced than ever.

Here's an overview of the leaked battery capacities compared with last year's specs (eSIM models):

  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 5567mAh
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 4288mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: 5088mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro: 4252mAh

As seen above, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery capacity will increase by roughly 10% over the previous generation. The iPhone 18 Pro's battery capacity is essentially unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro.

Both new models will benefit from efficiency gains in the A20 Pro and C2 modem, delivering better battery life. But if you're still torn between the two, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery advantage will stand out more than in previous years.

One trade-off for the larger battery is that the device will be heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro.

Another potential difference lies in the camera. Of course, we'd hope both Pro models share the same feature set. But last autumn, a credible leaker mentioned that the upcoming variable aperture system may be exclusive to the Pro Max.

We haven't seen other sources corroborate this yet. But Mark Gurman has said this will be a year of particularly big camera upgrades, so it wouldn't be out of the question for Apple to reserve at least one change for its larger, more expensive model.

Are you a Pro or Pro Max user? What differentiators could sway your choice? Share with us in the comments.
